recognize_zh: Prussian blue 染色的骨髓抹片顆粒（particle）中，佈滿大量粗大、成塊的藍色含鐵血黃素沉積，遠超過正常零星的細顆粒，表示骨髓鐵儲存明顯增加。
features: Bone marrow particle containing abundant coarse blue-staining hemosiderin granules and clumps
Iron deposits diffusely distributed throughout the particle, including large confluent aggregates
Pink-red nuclear fast red/safranin counterstain in the particle stroma
Image is out of focus; individual macrophages and erythroblasts (sideroblasts) cannot be assessed
describe_en: Prussian blue stain of a bone marrow aspirate smear shows a marrow particle heavily laden with coarse and confluent blue hemosiderin deposits, indicating markedly increased storage iron (high grade). The image is out of focus, so sideroblastic iron in individual erythroid precursors and ring sideroblasts cannot be evaluated. Findings are consistent with marked iron overload; correlation with serum ferritin, transferrin saturation and transfusion history is required to determine the cause.

ddx.vs: Normal marrow shows only small scattered blue granules within a few macrophages rather than coarse confluent deposits filling the particle.
Inflammation increases macrophage storage iron but usually to a lesser degree, with reduced sideroblasts and low transferrin saturation.

ddx.dx: Ring sideroblast disorders (MDS-RS, congenital sideroblastic anemia)
ddx.vs: These require identification of erythroblasts with perinuclear iron granules encircling the nucleus, which cannot be assessed on this particle view.
Precipitate lies on top of the smear in a different focal plane and also appears outside cells and particles, whereas hemosiderin is confined to the particle and macrophages.
